How to Protect and Manage a Texas Home During Probate: Construction Projects, Smart Home Systems, and Essential Estate Planning Tips

When a loved one passes away, probate can suddenly place a heavy list of responsibilities on an executor or family member. And for many Texans, the most valuable—and most complicated—asset to manage during probate is the home.

But today’s Texas homes aren’t simple structures.
They often include:

  • Ongoing or unfinished construction

  • Smart home systems

  • Digital locks and cameras

  • WiFi-dependent thermostats and lighting

  • Energy-efficient tech and automation

  • Indoor/outdoor AV installations

This technology helps homeowners in life, but it can create real challenges during probate if not handled properly.

In this guide, we break down exactly what Texas families need to consider when managing a home during probate—and how proper estate planning can protect the home’s security, value, and legal stability.

1. Understand the Executor’s Responsibilities for the Home

During probate, the executor must:

  • Secure the property

  • Maintain utilities

  • Protect the home from damage

  • Keep insurance active

  • Continue necessary repairs

  • Manage contractors or halt projects safely

  • Maintain smart devices and security settings

Probate can take months. During that time, the home must remain protected and functional—especially in Texas, where heat, humidity, and storms can quickly damage an unmaintained property.

2. Handling Construction Projects or Renovations During Probate

Many homeowners begin construction or remodeling projects shortly before they pass away. Others have ongoing upgrades, repairs, or additions in progress.

During probate, construction may need to:

  • Continue to preserve the property

  • Pause until the executor has authority

  • Restart under new agreements

  • Be formally reviewed for quality and safety

An executor cannot simply “let the contractor continue” without legal authority. Contracts, payments, and inspections must be properly documented.

For families who need help evaluating, completing, or planning construction during probate, Royal Coastal Builders offers professional support for remodeling, home building, and structural assessments across Texas.

They can help ensure any ongoing or needed construction work maintains—and does not jeopardize—the value of the estate.

3. Smart Home Systems: A Hidden Challenge During Probate

Texas homeowners increasingly rely on smart technology, including:

  • Smart locks

  • Doorbell cameras

  • WiFi lighting

  • Security systems

  • Thermostats

  • Smart gates and garage systems

  • Whole-home audio and AV setups

But these systems are tied to accounts and digital permissions, not just hardware.

After a homeowner passes away, problems may arise if:

  • No one has access to the apps

  • Passwords were never shared

  • Two-factor authentication (2FA) is required on a deceased person’s phone

  • The WiFi network disconnects

  • Monitoring subscriptions expire

This can leave the executor unable to:

  • Enter the home

  • Adjust climate control

  • Maintain security

  • Retrieve important camera footage

  • Reset or transfer devices

Specialized smart home companies like Intech Solutions help families access, reset, or reconfigure smart home systems so the executor can maintain security throughout probate.

4. Maintaining Utilities and Smart Infrastructure

A modern home cannot function—or stay safe—without:

  • Electricity

  • Internet

  • WiFi network access

  • Security and monitoring services

Interruptions in service can:

  • Disable security cameras

  • Break the smart lock system

  • Shut down thermostats or HVAC controls

  • Create mold and humidity issues

  • Interrupt irrigation or exterior lighting

  • Cause safety hazards

Executors should contact utility companies early, keep accounts active, and ensure smart home networks remain operable to protect the home.

5. Insurance Updates and Liability Protection

Texas homeowners’ insurance must be updated during probate to reflect:

  • A vacant property

  • An executor acting on behalf of the estate

  • Ongoing construction or remodeling

  • Smart security systems that reduce risks

Failing to notify the insurer can result in denied claims or gaps in coverage.

Additional coverage may be needed for:

  • Contractor liability

  • Theft or vandalism

  • Storm damage

  • Water leaks or HVAC failure

Probate homes are vulnerable—especially when vacant for long periods.

6. Estate Planning Steps That Prevent Major Problems Later

Homeowners can make probate dramatically easier by planning ahead.

A proper estate plan should address:

  • Who will have access to the home

  • Instructions for incomplete construction

  • Smart home passwords and digital access

  • Utility account transitions

  • Plans for selling or transferring the property

  • Trust-based ownership to avoid probate delays

  • Powers of attorney for emergencies

For families wanting to update their estate plan or prepare their home for the future, The Lange Firm helps Texans create wills, trusts, and probate strategies tailored to modern homes and today’s technology.

7. When to Contact a Probate Attorney

You should speak with a probate attorney if:

  • A home is left without clear instructions

  • There are ongoing construction projects

  • The property includes extensive smart home systems

  • Heirs disagree about repairs or upgrades

  • The home must be sold quickly

  • There’s uncertainty about access or liability

  • You’re the executor and unsure of your responsibilities

A well-handled probate protects both the property and the family’s peace of mind.

Final Thoughts: Managing a Texas Home During Probate Takes More Than Keys and Paperwork

Today’s homes are more complex than ever—featuring advanced construction, technology, and digital infrastructure. Probate must account for all of it.

By understanding:

  • Construction obligations

  • Smart home system management

  • Utility requirements

  • Insurance adjustments

  • Access control

  • Estate planning

…families can protect the home’s value and ensure a smooth probate process.

With smart builders, tech partners, and the right legal guidance, Texas homeowners—and their loved ones—can navigate probate with confidence and clarity.
